title: Bio: Detailed melanoma vaccine results
summary: Two multi-outlet clinical developments qualify: the existing detailed Phase 3 Moderna–Merck melanoma-vaccine results and new Phase 3 topline results for AbbVie’s lutikizumab. CAR-T, peptide-therapy, NAC, and NAD+ candidates in this collection were individual papers or trial-registry records without independent outlet coverage of a clinical or regulatory development.

stories.headline: A novel mRNA cancer vaccine helps reduce the chances of melanoma patients' tumors returning
stories.dek: Detailed Phase 3 results for intismeran autogene plus pembrolizumab showed reductions in recurrence and distant metastasis endpoints versus pembrolizumab alone.
tldr: Moderna and Merck reported detailed INTerpath-001 results for intismeran autogene combined with pembrolizumab in patients with resected stage IIB-IV melanoma.
The companies reported a 42% reduction in recurrence or death risk and a 38% reduction in distant metastasis or death risk compared with pembrolizumab alone.
Overall survival and regulatory review remain open, and the findings do not establish an approval decision or a treatment recommendation.

body.text: Moderna and Merck released detailed results from INTerpath-001, a Phase 3 study of intismeran autogene, an individualized mRNA-based therapy, given with pembrolizumab after surgery for stage IIB-IV melanoma. The comparison group received pembrolizumab alone. [1][2]

The trial enrolled more than 1,100 patients, and the companies had previously announced that it met its recurrence-free survival and distant metastasis-free survival endpoints. The newly reported results supplied the numerical detail ahead of a planned presentation at the European Society for Medical Oncology meeting. [1][2][3]

The reported combination reduced the risk of recurrence or death by 42% and the risk of distant metastasis or death by 38% versus pembrolizumab alone. Reuters reported that the analysis covered the first two years after treatment; AP also reported that the combination was tested as an addition to standard follow-up immunotherapy. [1][2]

The reported endpoints do not resolve overall survival, longer-term outcomes, or the eventual regulatory decision. These results concern a specific post-surgical melanoma population and investigational combination; further follow-up and regulator review remain necessary. [1][3]

stories.whyItMatters: The detailed readout moves the program beyond a topline announcement by quantifying recurrence and distant-metastasis outcomes in a late-stage trial. Whether those endpoint gains translate into longer survival, broader use, or regulatory approval remains unsettled.
stories.editorNote: Results cross-checked across AP, Reuters, and STAT. No clinical advice; overall survival and regulatory status remain open.

stories.headline: AbbVie Announces Topline Results from the Phase 3 INTREPID Trial Showing Lutikizumab Significantly Improved Signs and Symptoms of Disease in Patients with Hidradenitis Suppurativa
stories.dek: AbbVie said lutikizumab met the Phase 3 trial’s primary endpoint, while independent coverage noted the response advantage over placebo was narrower than some expectations.
tldr: AbbVie said its Phase 3 INTREPID study of investigational lutikizumab met the HiSCR75 primary endpoint at Week 16 in hidradenitis suppurativa.
The company reported response rates of 31.4% with lutikizumab and 23.4% with placebo among 1,400 participants.
Further 36-week data are expected in 2027 and will inform planned regulatory submissions; lutikizumab is not approved.

body.text: AbbVie announced topline Phase 3 results for lutikizumab, an investigational IL-1α/IL-1β antagonist, in adults and adolescents with moderate to severe hidradenitis suppurativa. The INTREPID trial randomized 1,400 participants and met its primary endpoint, the company said. [1][2]

At Week 16, 31.4% of participants receiving lutikizumab achieved HiSCR75, compared with 23.4% receiving placebo; AbbVie reported p≤0.001. HiSCR75 measures at least a 75% reduction in abscesses and inflammatory nodules without an increase in abscesses or draining fistulas. [1][2]

AbbVie also reported that the trial met eight ranked secondary endpoints, including measures of skin pain and disease flares. Fierce Biotech described the treatment-placebo difference on the primary measure as narrower than expected, underscoring that endpoint success does not itself establish comparative clinical value or approval. [1][2][3]

The company said additional results from a 36-week blinded extension are expected in 2027 and will be used to support planned regulatory submissions in the second half of that year. Lutikizumab remains investigational, and the cited materials do not establish a regulatory decision or long-term outcomes. [1][2]

stories.whyItMatters: The result advances a late-stage immunology program in a condition with limited treatment options, while the modest absolute response difference and pending longer follow-up leave the size and durability of benefit to be assessed. Regulatory review has not begun on the basis of these topline results.
stories.editorNote: Company-reported endpoints and percentages were checked against Fierce Biotech and STAT coverage. Results are investigational; no treatment guidance is offered.
